components.css: .ds-note-list { display: grid; gap: 2px; max-width: 300px; font-family: var(--font-ui); color: var(--fg); } .ds-note { display: grid; gap: 0.25rem; width: 100%; padding: 0.625rem 0.75rem; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: var(--radius-md); background: none; color: inherit; font: inherit; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color var(--duration-fast), border-color var(--duration-fast); } .ds-note:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--fg) 5%, transparent); } .ds-note[aria-current="true"] { border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 45%, transparent); background: var(--accent-soft); } .ds-note:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-note-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.375rem; min-width: 0; } .ds-note-title { flex: 1; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; font-size: var(--text-sm); font-weight: 750; letter-spacing: -0.005em; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-note-title.is-untitled { font-weight: 600; color: var(--muted); } .ds-note-star { flex: none; display: inline-flex; color: var(--accent); } .ds-note-snippet { display: -webkit-box; overflow: hidden; font-size: 0.78125rem; line-height: 1.45; color: var(--muted); -webkit-line-clamp: 2; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; } .ds-note-meta { display: flex; gap: 0.3rem; font-size: 0.71875rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--muted); }

narrative.overview:
NoteWren is a writing tool first, and the system is arranged so the words on the page stay central. Every control, label and heading is set in Manrope, a bold geometric sans. The note itself, its title and its body, is set in Source Serif 4. That split is the main expressive device: the interface speaks in one voice and the writing in another. Surfaces are warm paper neutrals separated by hairlines and small tonal steps. Colour is held back for actions, selection and status.

The identity sits alongside the interface. The supplied geometric wren, with its upright exclamation-mark tail and wing cutout, is drawn in ink on cream with terracotta as the identity accent, and moss and slate blue as secondary tiles. The wing and eye are true transparent holes in a compound path, so the bird works on any background. All shipped brand assets are SVG.

Density follows the platform. The reference site keeps its buttons, fields and section links at a 44px minimum height. The desktop mockups are deliberately compact, close to native macOS and tiled Linux sizing, so their icon buttons, search field and sidebar rows are smaller than 44px. This repository is a React 19 and TypeScript reference of tokens, components and mockups for a planned Tauri 2 app with a Rust core. Mockup notes are sample content held in memory for the session only: edits, new notes, theme and selection reset on reload. Storage, authentication and sync belong to the future native app and do not exist here.
keyCharacteristics: Two typefaces with fixed jobs: Manrope for the interface, Source Serif 4 for the writing.
Warm off-white light theme and warm green-grey dark theme, swapped by role variables.
A deeper clay action colour, separate from the identity terracotta.
Flat chrome built from hairlines and tonal surfaces; one shadow token for floating frames.
Small radii on controls, pills for chips and mobile actions.
Status always shown with words as well as colour.
A wren mark with real negative space, inheriting `currentColor`.

rules.name: The Two Terracottas Rule
rules.body: Identity terracotta (#d96545) belongs to the mark, app tiles and the default Omarchy frame. Interactive elements use the clay action role, never the identity hex.

rules.name: The Theme Swap Rule
rules.body: Components reference role variables (`--accent`, `--surface`, `--fg`), never theme hexes. Setting `data-theme="dark"` on the root element swaps the roles; identity colours stay fixed. The theme is chosen by the header toggle and is not read from the operating system preference.

rules.name: The OS Theme Rule
rules.body: On Omarchy, the app follows the desktop theme. A picker above the Omarchy mockup ("OS theme") offers NoteWren's own palette plus seven Omarchy palettes copied by hand from their `themes/<name>/colors.toml` files: Tokyo Night, Catppuccin, Gruvbox, Nord, Osaka Jade, Matte Black and Flexoki Light. `omarchyThemeStyle` in `src/components/omarchyThemes.ts` maps a palette onto the same role variables and the `--nwm-frame-*` variables as an inline style on `.nwm-omarchy`, so the waybar, active window border, list, editor and controls follow it with no component changes. Omarchy's `muted` is its divider colour and becomes `--border`; the palette accent becomes both `--accent` and `--focus`. The header light/dark toggle swaps roles for the whole page; the OS theme overrides them inside the Omarchy frame only, and "NoteWren" removes the override. This is a session-only preview of how a native Omarchy build would inherit the OS theme. That build would read the active theme's `colors.toml`; the mockup only simulates it with the copied list.

rules.name: The Words Not Colour Rule
rules.body: Every status carries a text label. Colour only reinforces it.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Manrope runs the interface. Source Serif 4 appears only for the writing: note titles and bodies on the page, and the prose specimen.

rules.name: The Tight Headings Rule
rules.body: Manrope tightens as it grows: -1.55px at display, -0.6px at headline, -0.045em on the wordmark. Body and label text keep normal tracking. Uppercase is limited to small overlines.

rules.name: The Page Measure Rule
rules.body: The writing page never exceeds 42.5rem, or 46rem in focus mode.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only floating frames get `--shadow-window`. Everything inside them sits on borders and tonal surfaces.

rules.name: The Real Cutout Rule
rules.body: Wing and eye are holes in a compound path. Never paint a cream or white shape over the bird to fake them.

dos: Do use the clay action role (`--accent`, #a64028 light, #f0a084 dark) for every interactive accent, and keep identity terracotta (#d96545) for the mark, app tiles and the default Omarchy frame.
Do keep `.nwm-omarchy` and the waybar on the `--nwm-frame-*` variables so OS palettes can recolour them.
Do set note titles and bodies in Source Serif 4 and everything else in Manrope.
Do reference role variables so `data-theme="dark"` swaps colours without component changes.
Do pair every status colour with a text label, as the Offline, Pending changes, Conflict and Up to date badges do.
Do keep one primary button per task, with a verb-led label.
Do separate regions with 1px hairlines and tonal surfaces, and reserve `--shadow-window` for floating frames.
Do keep the writing page within 42.5rem (46rem in focus mode).
Do use 140ms for control feedback and 220ms for view changes, with `--ease-out`, and honour reduced motion.
Do label anything in the mockups that could be mistaken for a working feature, such as the preview pill, the footnote and the "example" status items.
donts: Don't put white text on identity terracotta for interface buttons; use the clay action colour.
Don't fake the wren's wing or eye with a painted cream or white shape; they are transparent holes.
Don't stretch, rotate, recolour in gradients or redraw the bird, and don't set it on detailed backgrounds.
Don't use Source Serif 4 for controls, labels or navigation.
Don't describe every control as having a 44px target or the system as WCAG compliant; desktop mockup controls are intentionally compact.
Don't imply that mockup content is stored or synced; it lives for the session only.
Don't animate the writing page while someone types.
